newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, pondering stability.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat, pondering stability.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds mainly were flat in early morning trade on Friday as the market pondered whether the economy had entered a new and stable period after the latest data showed little inflation.

An initial firming after news that Producer Prices in June fell 0.01 percent, while the ex-food and energy rate rose 0.1 percent, bonds retreated after bonds hitting resistance, only to edge up once more. The near-term outlook appeared fairly stable.

"In terms of a market move, I don't look for the market to do anything," a trader said. Later, he added: "You really have no inflation, the economy is growing at a sustainable pace, the long bond belongs at 6.50 percent; it should not go any higher, it should not go any lower."
A drop in secondary market supplies was aiding municipal bond prices, a factor that looked likely to help them remain strong vis a vis Treasury bonds.

Yet the possibility that municipal bonds might outpace Treasury bonds was one of the risks that traders said could eventually end this sunshine period of recent gains. "The only thing that would be bad is that if we continue to rally higher, that would bring in refundings, bring in more supply," a trader said.

While how far yields would have to fall to make a refunding attractive varies for each issuer, the trader added that a fall in the 30-year, Treasury bond's yield to 6.25 percent or even six percent would spark a huge rise in refundings.
Activity in the secondary market was muted Friday as a number of players appeared to be getting an early start on the weekend.
The Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, a yardstick of this market, remained at just over $1 billion, a level considered fairly lean.
New issuance for next week was tentatively estimated to total around $1.716 billion with 109 issues, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
The competitive calender added up to around $700,000 in 73 sales, while the negotiated calender totaled $1.01 billion in 36 offerings.
In the secondary market, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, Sanitary Authority Sewer Revenues of 2024, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.51 percent, NET, down one basis point.
And Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2021, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.45 percent, NET, unchanged.
